RFK Jr. is exactly right to challenge NIH’s bloated bureaucracy and misplaced priorities. Venatorx Pharma’s reliance on NIH grants highlights the problem—taxpayer dollars funneled into Big Pharma partnerships that prioritize profits over patients. The real issue? NIH’s $47 billion budget fuels a revolving door between regulators and drug companies, with indirect costs padding university admin bloat instead of actual research. 

Cutting bureaucratic fat isn’t “illegal”—it’s overdue. Every dollar wasted on redundant studies or overpaid consultants is a dollar stolen from frontline medical innovation. The court blocking reforms proves the swamp protects its own. NIH’s 60,000 annual grants include millions for frivolous projects while critical treatments get delayed. 

Real solutions demand transparency: audit every grant, slash indirect cost scams, and redirect funds to breakthrough therapies—not corporate handouts.
